To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a bright deep‐red emissivematerial with AIE feature is synthesized, which is further encapsulated into NPs for deep‐tissue 3PF brain angiography with the largest penetration depth in ever reported AIE NP‐based 3PF imaging.
the deep‐red emissivity, good photostabilty, high biocompatibility, and large penetration depth of the TPATCN NPS make them a promising candidate for 3PF imaging in the brain.

a deep‐red AIE luminogen TPATCN is synthesized, and then TPATCN is encapsulated within F‐127 to generate NPs for in vivo three‐photon imaging of the mouse brain vasculature, with a penetration depth as large as 875 µm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of deep‐red 3PF AIE NPs with high chemical stability and biocompatibility for deep‐tissue imaging.
the development of a new class of bright AIE nanoparticles with F127 encapsulation, for deep‐tissue 3PF brain angiography.

the preparation of a new type of deep‐red emissively AIE NPs with excellent biocompatibility, which are utilized to realize deep‐tissue 3PF imaging in brain angiography, and further to realize multichannel nonlinear imaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a new class of AIE NPs for deep‐tissue 3PF imaging, with high brightness, chemical stability, and biocompatiblity.
the deep‐red emissivity and the excellent biocompatibility of TPATCN NPSs make them a promising platform for deep‐tissue 3PF intravital brain imaging.
the TPATCN‐F127 nanoparticles were successfully prepared, and the TPATCN Nps exhibited excellent three‐photon fluorescent (3PF) properties, which could be used for in vivo 4D brain imaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a deep‐red AIE luminogen, and then encapsulated the luminogen within a polymeric shell to form NPs for in vivo deep‐tissue 3PF imaging.
the TPATCN NPSs with AIE feature are successfully applied for deep‐tissue 3PF imaging in vivo, which is the first report for AIE nanoparticles to be used in vivo 3P imaging.
we have prepared deep‐red emissively bright AIE nanoparticles with F‐127 encapsulation for deep‐tissue three‐photon intravital brain angiography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a deep‐red AIE‐active luminogen TPATCN, which can form nanoparticles with bright 3PF emission.

the deep‐red emissiveness of TPATCN, the bright three‐phosphorescence of TPATCN NPS, and the high penetration depth of the 3PP fluorescence imaging of the brain vessels will be helpful for the study of the structure and function of the brain in vivo.
the deep‐red AIE NPs are highly suitable for deep‐tissue 3PF imaging, which may provide an alternative way for deep‐tissues imaging in the future.
